instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: Nova Analytics.tech is a specialized biotech company focused on developing novel monoclonal antibody therapies for complex autoimmune diseases, leveraging its lead candidate in Phase II clinical trials.
answers.pastInitiatives: We installed IoT sensors on 40% of our production equipment to monitor utilization and predict failures. The pilot showed a 15% reduction in unplanned downtime on instrumented machines. We now have a business case approved for full fleet rollout, but procurement and integration with our legacy maintenance system are proving more complex than anticipated.
answers.strategicGoals: We operate in a consolidating market where competitors are merging to gain economies of scale. Our independent position is increasingly vulnerable. We need to proactively strengthen our competitive positioning either by deepening our specialization in high-margin niches where scale matters less, or by building platform-like switching costs that make our offering stickier for existing customers.
answers.additionalContext: The company recently secured a partnership with a major academic institution to pilot novel diagnostic markers, signaling an attempt to diversify revenue streams outside of traditional antibody sales. Currently, internal communication across geographically dispersed R&D and commercial units often suffers from siloed data access.
answers.teamSize: We have a dedicated innovation squad of 8 people — 4 engineers, 1 data scientist, 1 UX designer, 1 product manager, and a part-time business analyst. This team operates with its own sprint cadence separate from the core product teams and has an allocated annual innovation budget. They report progress quarterly to the executive committee.

opportunities.title: Hyper-personalized Biomarker Integration via Liquid Biopsy
opportunities.rationale: By integrating advanced AI screening with real-time circulating tumor/disease biomarkers (liquid biopsy), Nova can rapidly personalize treatment protocols, creating a high barrier to entry for competitors. This leverages the existing Phase II data efficiently without requiring entirely new therapeutic modalities.

first_actions: Establish a cross-functional task force (R&D/Data Science) focused on liquid biopsy biomarker validation.
Allocate $150k for initial small cohort testing and data pipeline development.
execution_plan.success_metric: Achieve a 30% increase in biomarker-driven patient response rates in the pilot phase.
milestones: Q3: Finalize protocol and secure funding for Phase I liquid biopsy integration.
Q4: Pilot completion and internal ROI analysis.

opportunities.title: Decentralized, AI-Driven Antibody Design Platform
opportunities.rationale: Move beyond candidate screening into developing a proprietary platform that autonomously designs novel antibody structures optimized for specific autoimmune targets. This would create significant switching costs and position the company as an innovator defining the next generation of therapeutic discovery.

first_actions: Invest $500k in high-performance computing (HPC) clusters dedicated to generative AI for protein design.
Begin exploratory intellectual property mapping for novel binding domain architectures.
execution_plan.success_metric: Submission of one patent for a novel antibody scaffold generated entirely by the platform.
milestones: Q1-Q2: Build and validate core generative AI module.
Q3: Prototype successful design cycle generating viable candidates.

next_steps.action: Formalize the 'Bold' radical project proposal (AI Antibody Design) and secure dedicated funding from the formal committee.
Conduct a comprehensive review of cross-silo data protocols to enhance information flow between R&D and Commercial teams, addressing current digital maturity gaps.

key_weaknesses: Rigid internal process for mid-cycle innovation funding slows down agile pivots necessary in a fast-evolving biotech market.
Low digital maturity (Level 3) leads to inefficient data silos, hindering the integration of complex AI screening tools with legacy operational systems.
Over-reliance on traditional antibody discovery pathways risks being outpaced by competitors focusing solely on platform technology and novel modalities.
